articles.body:
I figured, if I'm going to start somewhere, I might as well start with the story that started all of this.

*The Last Druid.*

It's a little strange to look at it now. What was once just an idea sitting somewhere in the back of my head has somehow become a completed novel, a sequel in progress, and an entire world I have absolutely no intention of leaving anytime soon.\
But it certainly didn't start out that way.\
In fact, looking back at where it all began, I'm not entirely sure how I managed to get from there to here.

So, let's go back to the beginning.



### Where the idea came from

I’ve always been a bit of a dreamer, creating stories in my head, both epic and sentimental. And while I have written a lot of stories when I was still a young teenager, none of them ever made it somewhere. \
*(For good reasons, I might add. They were horrible.)*

And even though The Last Druid wasn't the first story I ever tried writing, it was the first one I worked hard enough on to actually get somewhere.

The first time I pictured the life of a druid in my head was, I believe, sometime in late 2023. Over the following year, I found myself thinking more and more about what the world around him might look like. But despite all the ideas running through my head, it wasn't until early 2025 that I actually started developing the story in detail.

Until then, I hadn't really considered whether I should write it all down or simply keep imagining and planning it in my head, like every other idea I'd had before.

I wasn't even sure if I would ever want to seriously try.

That was, until I had a chat with a very good friend of mine, and for the first time ever, told someone about the idea of Zane and his adventures.

He simply responded with something along the lines of:\
*“Fuck it, just do it. What are you waiting for?”*

And, well…\
I did.

He was my first real supporter, and I will forever be thankful for finally giving me that push I needed.

That friend, by the way, goes by the alias of Kallen. \
Yes, *that* Kallen.

Apparently, encouraging me to write a book comes with the risk of being immortalized in one.\
I'm sure he regrets nothing.



### When It Became *The Last Druid*

So, with the decision finally made, I sat down and started turning the world I'd been imagining for over a year into something I could actually put on paper.

And what can I say… all beginnings are rough.\
As was this one.

Not knowing where to even begin, I just went ahead and started planning out all the characters. The basic ideas for Zane, Melanie, and Kazumi formed rather quickly, while figuring out the details of Cynthia and Kallen turned out to be a much bigger challenge.

But soon enough, I thought I had every detail about every character planned out just right, so that no surprises could possibly hit me.

*Boy, was I wrong…*

And without much of an idea of how the journey would proceed, I just… started.

I never had to guide my characters. I just had to follow them.\
So, I did.

And they led me through all the beautiful moments they shared, the challenges they faced, and the milestones they reached.

All I can say is that they never failed to make me proud.

There was just one other thing that wasn't quite as settled as I thought.\
The name.

*The Last Druid* was never actually supposed to be the title of the book.

When I first started working on the story, it was little more than a project name, something to put at the top of the document while I figured out what I actually wanted to call it.\
Except I never did.

Somewhere along the way, *The Last Druid* stopped feeling like a placeholder and simply became the name of the story. I couldn't tell you exactly when that happened. At some point, I just stopped trying to replace it.

And now, after spending so long with it, I honestly can't imagine calling it anything else.

Apparently, some things knew what they wanted to be long before I did.



### What Changed Along the Way

I feel like I changed the opening chapters more times than I read them. In the very first version, Chapter One was… well, let's just say there was room for improvement.

Again, all beginnings are rough.

But after a few changes, I decided to keep it that way for a while, at least until I had a better idea of what the next few chapters would look like.

The first real roadblock hit around Chapter Six. \
I had the plot, I had the characters, I had shown enough to paint a picture. \
But for weeks, I didn't know how to proceed.

So, what did I do? Work at it until it was done? Fight it with everything I had?

No, I changed the opening again.

Duh.

Trying to achieve that improvement I was talking about, I added a prologue before Chapter One, one that, in retrospect, had absolutely no impact on how the story would continue.

But that wouldn't change again for a while, because at least I had finally managed to continue writing.\
Unfortunately, that was just the first roadblock of dozens.

And if I'm honest, to this day, I still haven't figured out a reliable way to get past them. At some point, it just starts working again out of nowhere.

But what I *did* figure out was how to finalize the opening for good.\
When did I figure that out?\
Exactly.\
When the book was complete.

But hey, better late than never, right?

### Looking Back

It's strange to think back to the beginning now.

When I first sat down to write *The Last Druid*, I didn't know whether I would ever finish it. I didn't know how long it would become, where exactly these characters would take me, or whether anyone other than a handful of people close to me would ever get to read it.\
Honestly, I wasn't even sure whether I could write a book.\
I just knew that I wanted to try.

And somewhere between all the rewrites, roadblocks, late-night ideas, scenes that seemingly wrote themselves and others that absolutely refused to, that attempt slowly turned into an actual novel.

There wasn't really one big moment where I suddenly thought, *I've got this.*\
Most of the time, I didn't.\
I just kept writing.\
And eventually, after spending so long following Zane and the others through their journey, I reached the end.

*The Last Druid* was complete.

Of course, “complete” turned out to be a rather generous word. There were still revisions to make, chapters to change, sentences to stare at for far too long, and an opening that apparently needed one final fight before I was allowed to call it finished.

But eventually, it was.

And now, looking at the finished manuscript while already writing *Rising Tide*, I sometimes have to remind myself that all of this started with an idea I wasn't even sure I wanted to put on paper.\
I'm incredibly glad I did.

There are plenty of things I would do differently if I were starting the book today. I suppose that's inevitable. I've learned a lot while writing it, and I'm still learning with every chapter I write now.\
But I don't think I'd want to go back and write it differently.

Because somewhere along the way, these characters stopped feeling like names in a document I had carefully planned out. Sekari stopped being nothing more than a setting in my head. And *The Last Druid* became the story that taught me that, apparently, I can actually do this.\
Which is probably a good thing.\
Because one book clearly wasn't enough.

*Rising Tide* is already making sure of that.

And to think, all it took to get here was one friend telling me:\
“Fuck it, just do it.”

Turns out, that wasn't such terrible advice after all.
articles.title: How The Last Druid Began
